description: Two versions of an interaction under the same events, for a person to judge. Says first whether anyone would notice the difference (imperceptible / subtle / clear, per property, with what changed: overshoot, settle time, position), then shows both: with `html`, real A/B filmstrips in two rows; otherwise both curves on one graph. If the change is below perception it proposes looking at an exaggerated version first.

a.description: The current version: { file }, { file, rev } (at a git revision) or { source, path? }. Not needed with `before`.

file.description: Path to a .nudg.json file, relative to the working directory.

path.description: With `source`: where the text would live, for resolving imports and labeling.

rev.description: With `file`: read it as it was at this git revision (HEAD, HEAD~1, a branch) instead of from disk, imports included.

source.description: The file's JSON text, to check before writing it. Imports resolve relative to `path`, or the working directory.

b.description: The changed version: { file }, { file, rev } or { source, path? }. Not needed with `before`.

file.description: Path to a .nudg.json file, relative to the working directory.

path.description: With `source`: where the text would live, for resolving imports and labeling.

rev.description: With `file`: read it as it was at this git revision (HEAD, HEAD~1, a branch) instead of from disk, imports included.

source.description: The file's JSON text, to check before writing it. Imports resolve relative to `path`, or the working directory.

before.description: Shorthand with `file`: compare the file at this git revision (HEAD, HEAD~1, a branch) with the file on disk; a and b are then not needed. Labels default to the revision and "now".

bundle.description: For a SwiftUI or Compose app: write the comparison (both versions compiled, the events, the verdict) to this .compare.json, for NudgCompare to play side by side on the app's own views. Put it in the app's resources or assets. Instead of html, url and out.

events.description: What happens, in time order. Each item is an event { "event": "track.tap", "t": 0.1 }, an input sample { "input": "track.drag.x", "value": 12, "t": 0.2 }, or a whole drag { "drag": "track", "t": 0.1, "until": 0.3, "dx": 20 } (down, dragstart, 60 samples per second, up, dragend).

dx.description: Horizontal travel of the drag, in logical units.

dy.description: Vertical travel of the drag, in logical units.

t.description: Seconds, or a string like "100ms". For a drag, when it starts.

file.description: With `before`: the file to compare across revisions.

frames.description: Evenly spaced frames when `at` is not given. Default 6.

html.description: The host page with the component's markup, when there is no running app. Gives real A/B filmstrips (needs Chrome) and writes a page the person should open: both versions playing side by side in a loop, with slow motion. Stills can't show feel; that page can. With html, a and b must both be files on disk (write the edited version first).

labels.description: Names for the two versions, default ["A", "B"].

layout.description: What the host would measure (0.4), reported at time 0: { "tab2.x": 96, "tab2.width": 88, "underline.x": 8 }. Measured values without it fall back to their base.

open.description: Open the side-by-side page in the person's browser. Default: once per session; later calls rewrite the same page and the open tab shows it after a reload. true forces a new tab, false never opens (NUDG_OPEN=false also turns it off).

out.description: Also save the picture here (.png; .svg for the graph).

page.description: Where to write that page. Default: next to `out` as .html, else in the temp folder.

properties.description: Properties to report, e.g. ["knob.x"]. Default: all.

reducedMotion.description: Play as a reduced-motion user would see it: short linear tweens, no kicks (0.3).

selector.description: With url: which element to snapshot. Default: the smallest element holding every bound target (a toggle's track with its knob).

start.description: Start in these states instead of initial, e.g. ["on"].

until.description: Last time to look at. Default: when everything has come to rest.

url.description: The running app's URL (or a local page). The component is snapshotted from it, styles and all, so no html file is needed: real A/B filmstrips, and the side-by-side page, on the real thing. Needs Chrome; a and b as files.

name: nudg_compare
title: Compare two versions
